messages:
Priya Rao: Hey team — onboarding PoppyTech. They're doing a pilot in AU/NZ and hitting 403s because their infra blocks our egress NAT. Customer asked for a temporary IP allowlist + a short QPS increase to validate UX. Renewal is on the line if pilot doesn't go smoothly. :worried:
Diego Martinez: thanks. do we have the exact IP ranges they need whitelisted and the QPS number?
Priya Rao: customer provided their firewall rules. they want our egress IPs whitelisted on their side, but they also asked if we can whitelist their proxy IPs on our edge for inbound control plane callbacks. Their requested QPS bump: from 150 -> 800 qps for 72h during the pilot window.
Priya Rao: their IP list: 203.52.128.0/22, 43.224.0.0/18, plus a static NAT 52.65.32.10. They want region restriction to ap-southeast-2.
Diego Martinez: ok. infra note: adding customer IP allowlist is low risk, but QPS bump might need rate window and auto-revoke. suggest policy: temp-rate-lift: 800 qps, window 72h, revoke after window. also pin to ap-southeast-2 capacity only.
Elliot Chung: capacity check — we can absorb +650 qps for 72h in ap-southeast-2 with current spare headroom but we should isolate to a single model shard to avoid cross-tenant impact. recommend limit to model:gptx-8k and add circuit-breaker at 1s p95 latency.
Samira Patel: anything billable here? PoppyTech is still on trial credits but willing to convert if pilot goes well. we should flag billing so finance can invoice any overages beyond credits. also capture feedback for renewal touchpoint.
Priya Rao: agreed. i'll add an enablement note and ask solutions to run a smoke test once allowlist is applied.
Diego Martinez: i'm going to apply the inbound allowlist and temporary rate policy now. command i will run:
```
rbw ops apply-allowlist --customer poppytech --direction inbound --ips "203.52.128.0/22,43.224.0.0/18,52.65.32.10" --region ap-southeast-2 --expires "2024-07-01T12:00:00Z"
rbw ops set-rate-policy --customer poppytech --region ap-southeast-2 --model gptx-8k --qps 800 --window 72h --auto-revoke true
```
Priya Rao: :crossed_fingers: please tag me when done so i can notify customer and run tests.
ops-bot: Command received: apply-allowlist (request-id 0a3f9c). Initiating change.
ops-bot: set-rate-policy queued (policy-id rp-9921).
ops-bot: allowlist applied — rule id al-7742 — scope: inbound, region ap-southeast-2, expires 2024-07-01T12:00:00Z.
ops-bot: rate policy active — policy id rp-9921 — qps 800 — window 72h — auto-revoke true.
Diego Martinez: done. smoke test next?
Priya Rao: yep i'll run a quick smoke now, pinging PoppyTech to run their end too.
Priya Rao: smoke test results: 5/5 requests success, latencies within expected. no 403s observed.
Samira Patel: great. i'll open a renewal playbook note: pilot successful so far; recommend account exec reach out 3 days before revoke to discuss committed capacity options and pricing. capture feedback: they mentioned wanting clearer docs on region-specific egress and a one-click allowlist workflow.
Elliot Chung: i'll add a monitoring alert for error rate >1% or p95 latency >1s during the window so we can rollback proactively.
Priya Rao: thanks all — i'll update the customer ticket and schedule a follow-up sync on day 2 of the pilot. :calendar:
Diego Martinez: added follow-up in my calendar. closing this thread after we confirm auto-revoke worked.
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: revoke-check at 2024-07-01T12:05:00Z (check policy rp-9921).
